rationale: The profile is essentially featureless (no source lines, no function list), identifying this as the puzzle benchmark from SingleSource/Benchmarks/Game — a small, single-file, compute-intensive program dominated by tight hot loops, so I prioritize cheap, low-risk transformations and gate the expensive ones. SUB gets the highest gain weights because instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime and size while defeating pattern-based analysis, and SPLIT is similarly inexpensive and adds structural diversity; both get very low cost/risk weights so they apply broadly. FLA and BCF provide the strongest control-flow hiding but can measurably slow hot loops, so their gain weights remain high (encouraging application) while their RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are elevated to 0.55-0.60 so that functions with strong runtime-cost features temper the decision — heavy flattening lands on cold code, not inner loops. IBR gets moderate treatment as a mid-cost, mid-risk blend. ICALL and IGV carry the highest CorrectnessRisk weights (0.40/0.45) because indirect calls and global-variable indirection interact badly with the unknown calling structure of benchmark-style code with no visibility into its symbol usage, so they are considered but applied conservatively. Overall the table biases toward structurally diverse, low-overhead obfuscation with cost-aware gating of the heavyweight control-flow passes, which suits a small hot-loop benchmark where runtime blowup is the main practical constraint and correctness must be preserved without any feature data to steer per-function risk.
